sampling_model.design: \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,Z_i,X_i)\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P\), with fixed \(K\) and a fixed number of cross-fitting folds.
sampling_model.units: Independent study participants with bounded continuous outcomes and pretreatment covariates.
sampling_model.treatment: \(J_i\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\) is latent and ordered; \(A_i\) and \(Z_i\) are paired categorical measurements.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each training fold first fits one raw label-aligned product law without using unknown measurement supports, the true conditional Gram matrix, or its rank. It then thresholds and renormalizes both measurement matrices at the data-chosen \(\tau_{S,n}\), and recomputes every bridge, posterior, projection, and score object from that cleaned law. The Gram inverse retains fitted eigenvalues above the known analysis-class cutoff \(\varepsilon/2\).

body.tldr: For every fixed \(K\geq3\), the exact continuous-outcome canonical gradient is the product-bridge score minus a pointwise \(K^2\)-cell projection and one conditional Gram correction. Tangent-space completeness is supplied by the proved bounded differential lift. The implementable score now starts from one raw product fit, thresholds and renormalizes both measurement matrices without using their true supports, and recomputes every bridge and operator from that cleaned law. If the raw sup-norm error is \(o_P(\tau_{S,n})\), every true-zero cell is removed with probability tending to one and the bias is quadratic in the cleaned rates \(r_A+\tau_{S,n}\) and \(r_Z+\tau_{S,n}\). Efficient cross-fitted Gaussian and maximum-\(t\) inference follows under the displayed product and threshold rates.

project_justification.gap: The binary hidden-treatment literature characterizes efficiency but computes its continuous-outcome correction through a partition-dependent sequence, while categorical product-bridge work establishes validity without observed-data canonicality. Existing continuous three-proxy identification results also do not provide the measurable uniformly bounded differential inverse required to identify the full observed DQM tangent closure.
project_justification.niche: Fixed latent cardinality, quantitative three-view separation, common outcome support, and paired categorical measurements permit both exact inversion of the differentiated factor map and elimination of the infinite-dimensional outcome nuisance before a finite conditional Gram solve.
project_justification.fill: The bounded differential-score lift closes tangent-space completeness and supports the exact finite canonical projector. For implementation, the paper uses one non-oracle product fit, a known analysis-class Gram cutoff \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\), and a data-driven support-cleaning threshold. Thresholding and column renormalization remove true structural-zero measurement cells on a high-probability sup-norm screening event without assuming beta-min for positive cells; all posterior, bridge, and projector objects are recomputed from the cleaned law. The resulting remainder is quadratic in cleaned measurement errors. Proving that the specifically named global spline likelihood attains the needed primitive and uniform rates, modal-label stability, and cleaned half-margin feasibility remains an explicit open construction question.

body.related_work: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) are the closest theorem-level comparator: their Theorems 2--4 treat the binary observed tangent space and influence functions, and Supplement S8.2 obtains the continuous-outcome efficiency bound through a refining outcome partition. The present multilevel construction instead uses the exact \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^+B^{\mathsf T}\) and one conditional Gram solve. Bian, Zhou, and Cui (2026) supply the categorical inverse-feature product-bridge precursor, but not observed-data canonicality or the support-cleaned projected-score remainder. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009), Hu and Schennach (2008), and Deaner (2023) inform latent-factor identification; none supplies the measurable bounded differential inverse proved here. Tsiatis and Ma (2004) inform nuisance-score projection, Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2016) inform coherent repeated-measurement estimation, and Tsybakov (2009) informs the smooth sieve benchmark. None of those cited results establishes the specific spline-likelihood curvature, uniform modal-label selection, and cleaned half-margin feasibility left open here. The implementation uses neither a true measurement support nor a true Gram rank; design-known supports remain only an optional specialization.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The results apply to the declared quantitatively separated, two-sided pathwise-interior specialization, not to the full published Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen or Bian--Zhou--Cui classes. The bounded differential inverse uses the posterior and projection-Gram gaps, and the Gram selector uses the known analysis-class margin \(\varepsilon\). Support cleaning requires \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=o_P(\tau_{S,n})\); efficient inference additionally uses \(\tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4})\) and the explicit cleaned product remainder. H\"older membership by itself does not prove the global spline-likelihood curvature, sup-norm rates, uniform modal-label selection, or high-probability feasibility of all fitted half-margins.
body.honest_scope: Exact identification, tangent completeness, the finite projector, canonicality, strict variance reduction, the binary comparison, and the continuous witness hold on the declared fixed-\(K\), quantitatively separated, two-sided pathwise-interior model. Cross-fitted implementation uses neither unknown true measurement supports nor an oracle Gram rank: it support-cleans a raw product fit and selects Gram directions at the known cutoff \(\varepsilon/2\). Its inference theorem is conditional on the raw sup-norm screening rate, \(\tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4})\), and the displayed cleaned product rates. Establishing those rates and fitted feasibility for the named B-spline product likelihood is still open. Modal ties, local singularity, failure of common outcome support, and failure of the screening window remain outside delivery. The maternal-smoking application is prospective because the published six-bin study does not itself verify paired-proxy conditional independence or the quantitative separation conditions.
body.interpretation: The efficiency conclusion rests on equality with the full observed-data DQM tangent closure, not projection onto a convenient latent submodel. Non-oracle implementation has two separate stability devices. The known separated-model margin permits the spectral cutoff \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\). Unknown measurement supports are handled constructively: fitted probabilities at or below \(\tau_{S,n}\) are set to zero, each column is renormalized, and every downstream score object is rebuilt. On \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}\leq\tau_{S,n}\), all true zeros are exactly restored, while positive cells may also be removed without invalidating the bound because the total perturbation is only \(O(r_\infty+\tau_{S,n})\). Thus no beta-min condition is hidden. The price is a cleaned first-stage rate of order \(r+\tau_{S,n}\), not the raw \(r\) alone.
